questions.prompt: Which approach best applies variant-aware dependency resolution?
options: Model compatibility with typed variants and configurations, then inspect why Gradle selected each dependency.
Put all library dependencies in api
Allow release to consume debug by default
questions.answer: Model compatibility with typed variants and configurations, then inspect why Gradle selected each dependency.
questions.explanation: The correct approach preserves Gradle’s lazy model, explicit data flow, variant correctness, functional evidence and operability.

questions.prompt: A version catalog determines the final resolved dependency version.
questions.explanation: Using resolutionStrategy.force to silence a mismatch can select a binary or behavioural combination that no producer declared compatible.

questions.prompt: When should a library dependency use api rather than implementation?
questions.answer: When its types are intentionally part of the library’s public ABI and must be visible to consumers.
questions.explanation: The answer names the model property that makes the build behaviour predictable rather than relying on incidental script order.
